title: Static Pods
description: Static Pods are created and managed by the the kubelet daemon on each node, without the API server observing them. Kubelet watches each static pod and restart it if it fails.    Kubelet automatically tries to create a mirror pod on the Kubernetes API server to represent the static pods, so it will be visible on the API server, however the pods cannot be controlled from there.  Static Pods are created based on a web or local filesystem YAML files which kubelet observes for changes. An attacker can use the static pods manifest file to ensure that a pod is always running on a cluster node and prevent it from being changed or deleted from the Kubernetes API server.

data_components.name: File Creation
data_components.definition: File system creation or modification events on the kubelet's static pod manifest directory (default: /etc/kubernetes/manifests/), where an attacker writes a new YAML file to cause kubelet to start a persistent container outside API server control.
relevant_events: Linux auditd: audit rule on -w /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ -p wa -k static_pod_manifest - any write or attribute change to the directory
inotifywait: IN_CREATE or IN_MODIFY event on /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml or *.json
Falco: open_write with fd.name matching /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml by process not in [kubeadm, kubelet, known-upgrade-script]

data_components.name: File Modification
data_components.definition: Modification of existing static pod manifest files to alter the image, command, or security context of existing system pods (e.g., kube-apiserver.yaml, etcd.yaml), representing a high-impact persistence path.
relevant_events: Linux auditd: WRITE syscall on /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml or any existing manifest by non-kubelet process
File integrity monitoring alert: hash change on /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml
Git/version-control event: change committed to infrastructure-as-code static pod manifest files outside normal change window

data_components.name: Pod Creation
data_components.definition: Mirror pod creation events on the Kubernetes API server that represent kubelet-managed static pods. A new mirror pod with no corresponding Deployment or DaemonSet owner, running on a specific node, indicates a static pod was started.
relevant_events: Kubernetes audit event: pod creation where pod name ends with node hostname suffix (static pod naming convention, e.g., attacker-pod-node01)
Kubernetes event: pod with ownerReferences=[] and annotations['kubernetes.io/config.source']=file on a specific node
Kubernetes API: GET pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> showing pod with no Deployment/RS owner reference and suspicious image

vendor_detections.title: Falco: write to kubelet static-pod manifest path
vendor_detections.intent: Fire on any file write to the kubelet's static-pod manifest directory on a node. Static pods bypass the API server entirely, so audit-log-based detection cannot see them; only on-node syscall-level monitoring can.
vendor_detections.query:
- list: kubelet_static_pod_manifest_paths
  items: ["/etc/kubernetes/manifests/", "/etc/kubelet.d/"]

- rule: Write To Kubelet Static Pod Manifest Path
  desc: A file was created, modified, or renamed inside the kubelet's static-pod manifest directory by a process that is not the legitimate package manager or kubelet self-update path.
  condition: open_write
             and (fd.directory in (kubelet_static_pod_manifest_paths)
                  or fd.directory startswith "/etc/kubernetes/manifests/"
                  or fd.directory startswith "/etc/kubelet.d/")
             and not proc.pname in (dpkg, rpm, yum, apt, apt-get, kubeadm)
  output: >
    Static pod manifest written outside legitimate path
    (user=%user.name proc=%proc.cmdline file=%fd.name pid_ns=%proc.pid_ns container=%container.name)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [k8s, persistence, static_pod]
required_telemetry: Sysdig agent (or open-source Falco) deployed as a DaemonSet on every node
Modern syscall driver (eBPF CO-RE) loaded so file-write events on the host filesystem are observable from the agent's namespace-aware view
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Legitimate cluster-bootstrap tools (kubeadm, kubelet TLS bootstrap, OS package updates of kube-apiserver/kube-controller-manager static manifests) write to these paths. Whitelist by the parent process exact match.
vendor_detections.limitations: Falco must observe the host filesystem, not just the container's. On nodes where the agent runs in a strict-namespaced pod without host filesystem visibility, this rule never fires. The agent must be configured with appropriate hostPath access to /etc/kubernetes/.

vendor_detections.title: File-integrity-monitoring hunt over node /etc/kubernetes/manifests/
vendor_detections.intent: Hunt over file-integrity events shipped from each node into the lake. List every write to the kubelet static-pod manifest path, joined against a known-good manifest snapshot to surface anomalies.
vendor_detections.query:
-- HOST_FIM.PUBLIC.EVENTS: file-integrity events from host agents
-- K8S.REF.STATIC_POD_MANIFEST_BASELINE: known-good manifest digests per cluster
WITH writes AS (
  SELECT
    event_time,
    cluster_name,
    node_name,
    file_path,
    actor_process,
    actor_uid,
    file_sha256
  FROM HOST_FIM.PUBLIC.EVENTS
  WHERE event_kind IN ('write', 'create', 'rename')
    AND (file_path LIKE '/etc/kubernetes/manifests/%'
         OR file_path LIKE '/etc/kubelet.d/%')
    AND event_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT cluster_name, file_path, file_sha256 FROM K8S.REF.STATIC_POD_MANIFEST_BASELINE
)
SELECT
  w.*,
  CASE WHEN b.file_sha256 IS NULL THEN 'unknown digest' ELSE 'matches baseline' END AS digest_status
FROM   writes w
LEFT JOIN baseline b
    ON b.cluster_name = w.cluster_name
   AND b.file_path    = w.file_path
   AND b.file_sha256  = w.file_sha256
WHERE  digest_status = 'unknown digest'
ORDER  BY event_time DESC;
required_telemetry: Host-level FIM agent (auditd, osquery, Falco-to-lake, or commercial FIM) shipping file-write events to Snowflake
STATIC_POD_MANIFEST_BASELINE reference table populated and refreshed when legitimate manifest changes ship
vendor_detections.false_positive_considerations: Cluster-control-plane upgrade events change the static manifests for kube-apiserver / kube-controller-manager / kube-scheduler. Coordinate baseline refresh with the upgrade process, or pre-stage approved digests.
vendor_detections.limitations: FIM telemetry shipping from every node is operationally heavy. Many environments don't have it. Without it, static-pod creation is invisible.

mitre_cross_references.name: Container Service
mitre_cross_references.rationale: A static pod is a pod defined by a manifest file on a node's filesystem (/etc/kubernetes/manifests/) and managed directly by kubelet, not the API server. Placing a malicious manifest there creates a persistent container service that restarts automatically -- this is precisely the pattern T1543.005 (Container Service) covers: 'adversaries may create or modify container service configurations to survive system restarts.' Static pods are invisible to kubectl by design and constitute a stealth persistence mechanism.

mitre_cross_references.name: Escape to Host
mitre_cross_references.rationale: Writing a static pod manifest to /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ requires write access to the host node filesystem. An attacker who has escaped to the host (T1611) can plant a static pod manifest as a persistent backdoor. The sequence is T1611 (host escape) -> write manifest -> static pod becomes persistence. The Atomic Red Team T1611 test 2 explicitly demonstrates that host filesystem write is the outcome of container escape.
